label: the wrench (models/v_crowbar.mdl, models/p_crowbar.mdl, models/w_crowbar.mdl): a pipe wrench: red-painted handle worn to bare iron, a heavy toothed jaw

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_9mmar.mdl, models/w_357.mdl, models/w_satchel.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked B, D, A, D where the asset was D, B, D, A: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Against the brief's words (a pipe wrench, about 18 long, a red handle with a heavy toothed jaw), every one of the ten views reads as a wrench: a long handle with a box-shaped jaw at one end, nothing missing and nothing stuck out. The jaw is a plain block, a little squarer than a real pipe wrench's, which the brief does not ask for.

M2.reason: Measured 19 x 3.5 x 6.4 against the brief's 18 long, 5.5% off, inside the 15% band. Width and height are not given in the brief.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, down to the small: the red handle (sides.png, LEFT and RIGHT), the heavy jaw (sides.png, FRONT-LEFT and BELOW), and its teeth, four on the jaw's edge (TOP, BELOW, and in-hand.png, where all four are clear). The handle's end cap and the jaw's cross-hatched plate are also there. Nothing the brief names is missing.

M4.reason: The red handle is right, but the bare-iron areas read as pale, near-white grey (sides.png, LEFT and RIGHT: the striped bands on the handle; the jaw is flat white). Worn steel should read as darker, dull iron. The grey is off enough that a player would not take it for worn iron, though it is not a different material.

M5.reason: The worn stripes on the handle, the cross-hatched grip plate on the jaw's face (sides.png, LEFT and TOP) and the red wearing through to grey (in-hand.png) are all there in their places, at a sharpness fit for the size shown. The brief asks for no more than this.

M6.reason: Scored 2 by the brief's line-up rule for this judge. In lineup.png the asset (D) stands out from the Valve guns and the pack, but the test was not caught; the measurement says it passed for one of the game's.

M7.reason: The world model lies flat on its side with the jaw at one end, the way a dropped wrench lies. The front is clear (the jaw faces forward in sides.png, FRONT-LEFT). The origin is not shown in the pictures, so this is judged from the lying pose alone.

M8.reason: SMAK's check gives no errors. 108 triangles, well under twice the median of Half-Life's own kind and size. In sides.png no face is open or floating: the handle's end cap and the jaw's back are closed in every view that shows them.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the asset is held larger and further left than the game's crowbar, its head filling the top of the frame and its jaw out of the picture at the bottom, so it does not sit where the original sits. In attack.png frame 1 the weapon is out of the picture, which is not leaving the hands, but no frame shows the hands, so keeping hold through the swing cannot be confirmed.
